subject: Post-demo debrief: SDK auth, routing, and response schema questions
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@portaldynamics.com>, Ivy Chen <ivy@portaldynamics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo debrief: SDK auth, routing, and response schema questions

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps and a handful of architecture/contract questions so our engineers can scope the integration.

Key recap:
- You liked the low-latency streaming and the ability to route specific tenant traffic to Dedicated pools.
- Use-cases: contextual chat for support agents (multi-turn), and an on-site search re-ranker for product docs.
- Priority: secure backend service integration (SSO), predictable per-request cost limits, and deterministic structured outputs from the model for downstream tooling.

Questions we need answered to prepare a short technical playbook for your team (can be high-level):
1) SDK and auth: you mentioned Python backend + Node frontend. Do you plan to authenticate backend calls via OIDC (service-to-service tokens) or do you prefer Redwood-issued API keys for server roles? Any constraints from security/compliance about ephemeral creds?

2) Routing and deployment: do you expect to route traffic to Redwood Dedicated by tenant, or are you planning to use the Hosted API with routing rules for high-priority tenants only? Do you need geo-based routing (EU/APAC)?

3) Structured outputs & tool calling: for agent workflows, do you need function/tool-calling style JSON structures (strict schema) or are you okay post-processing free-form chat output with a lightweight extractor? Example: a deterministic JSON payload to populate your case management system vs. an NLP parser.

4) Re-ranker & embeddings: for search quality, do you plan to store embeddings for the whole index and call a reranker (two-stage) on top of top-K? What latency SLOs for the re-rank path (e.g., 200ms vs 500ms)?

5) Request/response schema: important clarifications we need about token budgets and streaming semantics — specifically:
   - Are max_tokens limits meant to apply to the response only, or prompt + response combined?
   - Do you rely on stop sequences for terminating generation, and if so, are there multiple disjoint stop tokens we need to support?
   - Do you expect chunked streaming (partial tokens as they arrive) and to rely on the SDK to deliver a streaming end-of-message event?

If you can reply with short answers to the bullets above, we'll put together a 1-page architecture recommendation plus a sample request payload you can share with your infra team.

Attaching our demo notes and a rough recommendation checklist.

Attachments: [portal-demo-notes.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks — happy to hop on a technical call if that helps.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@portaldynamics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Ivy Chen <ivy@portaldynamics.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo debrief: SDK auth, routing, and response schema questions

Thanks Sean — great demo, especially the routing examples. Short answers inline, plus a few follow-ups.

1) SDK and auth: Backend will be on Python (FastAPI). We must integrate with our corporate IdP (OIDC) for service-to-service tokens. API keys are acceptable for prototype but not for production. We can do a short-lived token exchange if Redwood supports OIDC token exchange (or a token mint flow).

2) Routing and deployment: We want tenant-level isolation for our top 5 customers (Dedicated). The rest can go to Hosted. No immediate EU/APAC requirement — US first.

3) Structured outputs & tool calling: For agent automation (case creation, priority routing) we need deterministic JSON (tool-calling style) — fields must be stable. We cannot rely on free-form parsing for the production path.

4) Re-ranker & embeddings: Yes — two-stage. We'll run an ANN index (FAISS) and then do a lightweight model rerank on top-K. Target p95 latency for search path is <= 300ms. If reranker adds too much latency we'll consider async enrichment.

5) Request/response schema: a few sub-questions:
   - Token budget: we intend to cap end-user visible response tokens to 250, but prompts can be large (context window up to ~8k). So we need to confirm whether Redwood's max_tokens parameter is prompt+response or response-only.
   - Stop tokens: we use multiple stop markers ("\n---\n", a GUID marker, and sometimes the literal ") in templates). How does streaming handle stop detection? Do you send a terminal event or just stop sending tokens?
   - Streaming: yes, we prefer chunked streaming to start rendering tokens as they arrive in the UI. We also need token-level offsets for analytics (to map token index back to time for cost accounting).

If you can share an example request payload for both chat (multi-turn) and completions (single-instruction rerank prompt) and the recommended settings (max_tokens, stop, streaming: true/false), that would be ideal.

Thanks — happy to have Marissa schedule a technical deep-dive with your engineers.

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Search & Automation, Portal Dynamics
alex.johnson@portaldynamics.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@portaldynamics.com>, Ivy Chen <ivy@portaldynamics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo debrief: SDK auth, routing, and response schema questions

Alex — good questions. I pulled Karthik and our infra engineers into some short answers here so your team has something concrete to test. High level guidance below; we can provide a runnable Postman/Python sample in the tech sync.

Chat vs Completions
- Chat (multi-turn): use chat endpoints for agent workflows where you maintain conversation state, system messages, and incremental tool calls. Chat endpoints preserve role structure (system/user/assistant) and are optimized for multi-turn context.
- Completions (single-shot): use for re-ranker scoring or single-instruction tasks where you send the candidate and a short instruction template. Lower overhead and easier to parallelize.

Tokenization & max_tokens
- Redwood's max_tokens is applied to the response (generated tokens) by default for both chat and completions. The platform also enforces a combined context limit (prompt + response) based on the model's context window. We'll include this note in the sample payload.
- For your use-case: set max_tokens=250 for user-visible responses, and enforce a higher soft limit on prompt size server-side to keep total under model window.

Stop sequences & streaming semantics
- Stop tokens: supported as an array; server detects stop tokens during generation. Upon detecting a stop token the runtime finalizes the output and emits an end-of-message event.
- Streaming: chunked token streaming is supported. SDKs deliver partial tokens as they are generated and then emit a final 'done' event. Token offsets are available in the streaming frames for analytics (we can emit a running token_count).

Structured outputs / tool calling
- We recommend function/tool-calling for deterministic JSON outputs. The runtime validates the JSON schema where possible and can return a structured response. If you require strict post-validation, we can enable strict mode which rejects non-conforming generations and returns an explicit error for deterministic handling.

Embeddings & reranker guidance
- Typical pattern: ANN to surface top-K (k=50), then a lightweight model reranker over top-K to produce final ordering. To meet 300ms p95, put the ANN in a low-latency store (SSD-backed FAISS + warmed CPU) and run a quantized reranker on a small GPU pool or CPU-optimized model.

Sample recommendations (high-level)
- Chat agent: streaming=true, max_tokens=250, stop=["\n---\n", "<END>"]
- Re-ranker (completion): model=short-context-quant, max_tokens=32, streaming=false, prompt_template includes structured response instructions + candidate id for mapping.

Next steps:
- Karthik: can you run a 30-min tech sync tomorrow to walk the infra folks through OIDC flow and a sample streaming chat payload?
- Alex/Ivy: please confirm a 30-min slot (we've suggested a few times in the calendar link below).

Attaching a short checklist and our recommended request examples in the tech doc.

— Marissa
